reach.rationale: No experimental APIs or flags in application code, but one genuinely beta dependency (Nitro 3) runs the production build/server, and the entire framework stack (Start 1.169, Vite 8) stabilized within the last ~7 months — the Start core just days ago. That lands squarely on 'one or two, plus recently-stable APIs in central places.'

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:13 — the beta nitro plugin appears in exactly one file; app code never imports nitro
app/src/lib/server.ts:11-57 — all six createServerFn calls are wrapped in one module behind a withNotFound helper, so a server-function API change is a one-file fix
app/src/lib/api.ts:16-28 — all HTTP/data access isolated behind apiGet, and Start-framework surface area is confined to router.tsx and standard route files
containment.rationale: The risky pieces are maximally contained: the beta Nitro dep lives in vite.config.ts and package.json only, and framework touchpoints are wrapped in thin, centralized modules (server.ts, api.ts). Swapping the host or an API change is a one-file edit.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:13 + app/package.json:22 — nitro() is the documented replacement for the removed @tanstack/nitro-v2-vite-plugin per TanStack's 'Migrate from the Release Candidate' guide, and the only way to satisfy the spec's `npm start` node-server requirement with Start 1.169
app/src/lib/server.ts:27 — .validator() is the current stable API, not the removed RC-era .inputValidator(); the app tracks the release's canonical usage
app/src/routes/index.tsx:32 — staleTime: Infinity on a static catalog is a long-stable router option used for a real caching reason, not novelty
justification.rationale: Every non-stable or brand-new API buys something a stable alternative couldn't: there is no stable Nitro 3 yet and TanStack explicitly directs Start users to it for node hosting; nothing experimental is used gratuitously (no RSC, no middleware, no SSR experiments).

findings.issue: Production build and server (npm run build / npm start, node .output/server/index.mjs) run on Nitro v3 beta (^3.0.260903-beta); Nitro 3 only reached RC on 2026-10-29 and has no stable release, so breaking changes may still land
findings.suggestion: This is the path TanStack's own stable-release migration guide prescribes for node hosting, so it's defensible — but bump to the v3 RC promptly, watch the 'Upgrading from Beta' breaking-change notes, and pin the version rather than relying on a caret range over beta tags

findings.issue: The whole app rests on @tanstack/react-start 1.169.4, the first stable release (2026-10-13), so every central API (createServerFn, shellComponent) was an RC API 18 days ago
findings.suggestion: Spec-mandated framework, so nothing to change; budget for churn in the first few minor releases and track Start patch notes

findings.issue: resolve.tsconfigPaths is a Vite 8-era addition (stable, but only ~7 months old and off by default; some ecosystem docs still call it experimental-marked)
findings.suggestion: Fine as-is — it's what TanStack Start's path-alias guide recommends; just note it silently depends on tsconfig include patterns matching CSS files for the app.css import

summary: This is a conservative, current-release app: zero unstable_ or experimental_ APIs, no experimental config flags, and the exact stack the framework's October 2026 stable release prescribes, including the renamed .validator() server-function API. The single pre-stable dependency is Nitro v3 beta in the build/hosting chain, which is contained to vite.config.ts and package.json and is TanStack's documented path for a self-hosted node build. Residual risk is concentrated in how young the whole stack is (Start 1.169 stable Oct 13, 2026; Vite 8 stable March 2026), not in how the app uses it.
